seoTitle: Free Aspect Ratio Calculator: Resize and CSS Snippets
metaDescription: Simplify a width and height to its aspect ratio, scale to a new size, and copy CSS aspect-ratio and padding-hack code. Free, in your browser.
intro: Reduces a width by height pair to its simplest ratio, such as 16:9, and scales it to a new width or height. It also prints the CSS aspect-ratio rule, the padding hack and a Tailwind class.
why:
Resizing an image or a video without distorting it needs the ratio kept intact. Working out that 1920 by 1080 is 16:9, or what height a 1280 pixel wide version should have, is simple arithmetic that is easy to fumble when you do it quickly, especially with unusual sizes.

Enter the dimensions as 1920x1080 or 16:9. The tool reduces them, shows the decimal ratio and the megapixel count, then scales to a width or height you supply. Alongside the numbers you get ready-made CSS: the modern aspect-ratio property, the older padding-top percentage trick for browsers without support, and a Tailwind arbitrary class. All calculation runs in your browser.
howTo: Enter the dimensions as W x H or W:H, for example 1920x1080.
Type a new width or a new height to scale to.
Read the simplified ratio, decimal and megapixels.
Copy the CSS aspect-ratio, padding hack or Tailwind class.

faq.a: Two numbers separated by x, a colon, a slash, an asterisk or the multiplication sign, for example 1920x1080 or 16:9. Decimals are allowed. Anything else shows a hint about the expected format.

faq.q: How is the simplest ratio found?
faq.a: Both numbers are scaled to thousandths and divided by their greatest common divisor, so decimal sizes still reduce neatly. Odd sizes like 1366x768 give an awkward ratio such as 683:384.

faq.q: What is the padding hack for?
faq.a: Before the aspect-ratio property was supported everywhere, developers set padding-top as a percentage of the width to reserve a box of the right shape. The tool prints that value as well, for old browsers.

faq.q: Which new size does it calculate?
faq.a: If you give a new width it works out the height, and if you give a new height it works out the width. Set a field to 0 to skip it. If you fill both, you get both results.
